title: basic-auth CreateModelVersion: source run/model READ check must use proto-parsed runId/modelId, not raw body keys
answers: Why can a user create a model version from a run they cannot read when the REST body uses camelCase runId?
Where does basic auth decide whether a model-versions/create request may reference a source run or logged model?
How should a new field on model version create that references another resource be authorized?
Why does the model-versions/create validator parse the body through the proto instead of reading JSON keys?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_create_model_version, the before-request validator for POST /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/create. It runs for any create-model-version request that sets a source run or logged model (run_id/runId or model_id/modelId in the JSON body) and checks READ on that source before the handler anchors the new version to it.
Rule: Parse the body with _get_request_message(CreateModelVersion()), test presence with msg.HasField("run_id") and msg.HasField("model_id"), and authorize the bound values through _get_run_permission / _get_model_permission (via _can_read_model_version_source). Do not read raw request JSON keys: the proto JSON parser also binds the lowerCamelCase aliases, so a body carrying only runId or modelId skipped the READ check while the handler still used that id.
Symptom: An authenticated user with no READ on another user's run could create a model version pointing at that run through a registered model they own, then read the run's artifacts through that version, since artifact reads on a version are authorized only against the caller's own registered model.
Constraints: HasField keeps the rule that an explicitly empty id is denied rather than treated as absent. A non-dict body degrades to an empty message and falls through to the handler's own validation. The same proto-parse pattern is used by validate_can_log_metric, validate_can_log_batch and validate_can_update_run_or_logged_model; the registered-model/prompt update check still runs first.
applies: Basic-auth server authorization of POST model-versions/create source run and logged-model references; not for handlers that take no source id.
says: Users can register a model version from an experiment run they cannot view.
Prevent users from creating model versions referencing training runs they cannot read.
Unauthorized members can view private run artifacts by registering a new model version.
Model registry allows linking private experiment runs when saving new model versions.
Block unauthorized users from accessing another user's run outputs through the model registry.
search: In `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py`, `validate_can_create_model_version` checks source run and logged-model READ authorization for `POST /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/create` by parsing the request body into a `CreateModelVersion` protobuf message. Using `HasField('run_id')` and `HasField('model_id')` binds lowerCamelCase JSON aliases like `runId` and `modelId` so permissions are verified before anchoring the version. Explicitly empty IDs are denied, non-dictionary bodies fall through to handler validation, and this proto-parsing pattern also applies to `validate_can_log_metric`, `validate_can_log_batch`, and `validate_can_update_run_or_logged_model`. The rule applies to model version creation requests specifying a source run or logged model, with registered model authorization still running first.
